name: Ried im Oberinntal
kurzbeschreibung: Warm and welcoming community in the Oberinntal with an intact village structure and stunning hiking trails.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Ried im Oberinntal is located in the Landeck district at an altitude of 876 metres in the historic Oberes Gericht region on the right bank of the Inn River, counting around 1,310 residents. The community rests at the gateway to the Kaunertal valley, situated beneath the sunny mountain terrace of Fendels. Serving as a crucial junction along the ancient Roman Via Claudia Augusta and Reschen Pass road, Ried links the Upper Inn Valley with the alpine crossroads where Austria, Italy, and Switzerland meet. The town enchants visitors with its swimming lake, Late Medieval Schloss Sigmundsried castle, and direct cable car access to Fendels.

Geschichte

Ried was first recorded between 1115 and 1122 in the records of Reichenbach Monastery, with bronze age relics indicating ancient settlement. The municipal coat of arms bears a mythical basilisk, the heraldic crest of the medieval Lords of Ried. Around 1325, they erected a fortified tower which was purchased in 1471 by Duke Sigmund the Wealthy and expanded into the royal hunting seat of Schloss Sigmundsried. For more than four hundred years, it housed the regional district court. The Late Gothic parish church of St. Leonard was built between 1512 and 1526, receiving its Romanesque-style bell tower in 1550. Baroquised in the 18th century, it features a masterly high altar created by Michael Stämer in 1720 with sculptures by Andreas Kölle.

Anreise

Reaching Ried im Oberinntal is straightforward. By car, drivers proceed along the Inntalautobahn A12 to the Oberinntal junction near Landeck, pass through the toll-free Landeck Tunnel, and continue along the B180 Reschenstraße for 14 kilometres directly to Ried. Rail passengers arrive at Landeck-Zams main railway station along the Arlberg railway. From Landeck station, VVT regional bus line 210 runs every 30 minutes, reaching Ried in roughly 25 minutes with onward links to Nauders and the Kaunertal glacier.

Tipps

A favourite summer highlight is Lake Rieder Badesee, a 2.6-hectare natural recreation complex fed by mountain springs, featuring waterslides, sunbathing lawns, and the Bibis Wasserkraft adventure playground. Right beside the lake, the Ried-Fendels cable car ascends to the Fendels family mountain for alpine walking trails, family skiing, and floodlit tobogganing. Mountain bikers can challenge the Wildbachtrail downhill course, which crosses a daring 30-metre suspension bridge spanning the Fendler Wildbach gorge. Trekkers should explore the Anton-Renk-Weg trail leading to the Anton-Renk-Hütte refuge beside the roaring 150-metre Fallender Bach waterfall, while Schloss Sigmundsried hosts cultural exhibitions and concerts.
